text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Top Alliance for Democracy (Aford) official Machipisa Munthali has defected to the ruling United Democractic Front, hitting a raw nerve in relations between the UDF and Aford, which is in merger talks with the Malawi Congress Party.

- Former presidential economic advisor Kalonga Stambuli has been granted bail in his trial on charges of misappropriating funds from President Bakili Muluzi's International Appeal Fund for Clean Water.

- Finance and Economic Planning Minister Aleke Banda said the private sector and individuals in Blantyre should take advantage of a Southern African Development Community (SADC) heads of state summit in September to generate business by offering accomodation. Blantyre has just 32 hotel rooms and will struggle to accommodate the 500 delegates expected.
- Government sources alleged that three cabinet ministers benefited personally from President Bakili Muluzi's International Appeal Fund for Clean Water.
- Fraudsters are continuing to swindle financial institutions and most culprits go unprosecuted, Commercial Bank of Malawi chief executive Dennis Lawrence said.
- City councils are planning their own policing systems to enforce bylaws regulating minibus taxis.
- The September SADC heads of state summit has created panic over accommmodation and some delegates might have to stay in guest homes up to 200 km from the conference centre.
- The Civil Liberties Committee is raising money to buy drugs for inmates of Chichiri remand prison, which has been hit by an outbreak of dysentery and scabies.
